questions Obstacles: Explaining the architectural nuances of AI/ML projects clearly under time constraints.Round 4: Technical Interview 2Duration: 1 hour (Conducted exactly 1 hour after Technical After submitting the form, shortlisted candidates received an email inviting them to take the online assessment.Candidates who cleared the assessment received a call explaining the next steps. During the call, the recruitment team informed us about the interview schedule and instructed us to attend the technical interview in person at Target India's office in Manyata Tech Park, Bengaluru.Key Questions / Assessment:Around 35 MCQs covering Aptitude and Core Computer Science subjects.Two coding questions with Easy to Moderate difficulty.Technical Round Duration: Approximately 45–60 minutes Method: In-person Focus:The interview was primarily resume-driven. Most of the questions were based on the technologies, skills, and projects mentioned in my resume.Although I had applied for the Target India Apprenticeship Program, I was interviewed by a React Front-End Developer. The discussion focused mainly on my Computer Science fundamentals and project experience.Explain your resume.Walk me through your projects.Explain the four pillars of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP).What is Encapsulation?What is Abstraction?What is Inheritance?What is Polymorphism?Explain the OSI Model and its seven layers.Write a program to implement Bubble Sort.What is the time complexity of Bubble Sort?Write basic SQL queries.What are DDL, DML, and TCL commands?What are database transactions?Explain transaction management in DBMS.Questions based on the technologies and projects mentioned in your resume.Where are you from?What are your hobbies?Casual Discussion The interviewer was very friendly and made the interview conversational. Along with technical questions, he asked about my native place and my hobbies. When I mentioned cricket as one of my hobbies, we had a brief discussion about the IPL and the franchise I support.Obstacles:There were no major obstacles during the interview. The biggest takeaway was that every project, skill, and technology mentioned on the resume should be well prepared, as the interview was heavily based on the resume.Additional Information After the interview, it took approximately two weeks to receive an update. I received an email informing me that I had successfully cleared the interview process. A follow-up call was then scheduled, during which the recruitment team informed me that I would be receiving a Letter of Intent (LOI). A few days later, I received the official Offer Letter, and I joined the Target India Apprenticeship Program around 15–20 days after receiving the offer letter.Comment Corporate & Communications Address:A-143, 6th Floor, Sovereign Corporate Tower, Sector- 136, Noida, Uttar Pradesh (201305)Registered Address:K 061, Tower K, Gulshan Vivante Apartment, Sector 137, Noida, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, 201305Company About Us Legal Privacy Policy Careers Contact Us Corporate Solution Campus Training Program Explore POTDPractice Problems Blogs Upskill Courses Connect Tutorials Programming Languages DSAWeb Technology AI, ML & Data Science Dev Ops CS Core Subjects GATESchool Subjects Software and Tools Courses ML and Data Science DSA and Placements Web Development Data Science Programming Languages Dev Ops & Cloud GATEMongo DB Certifications Preparation Corner Interview Corner Aptitude Puzzles Gf G 160System Design@Geeksfor Geeks, Sanchhaya Education Private Limited, All rights reserved

Courses Tutorials Practice Jobs DSAPractice Problems C C++Java Python Java Script Data Science Machine Learning Courses Linux Dev Ops Share Your Experiences DSA Tutorial System Design Tutorial Aptitude Questions and Answers Web Development Technologies AI, ML and Data Science Tutorial Dev Ops Tutorial DSA to System Design Explore Smart India Hackathon 2025 Experience - Hardware Edition Last Updated : 26 Jun, 2026Hello, I'm Anushka Yadav | B.Tech CSE, IPS Academy, Indore Smart India Hackathon (SIH) is one of India's largest and most prestigious hackathons, where thousands of student teams compete to solve real industry and government problems. In December 2024, my team made it to the top 5 out of 500+ submissions in our domain — and represented our college at IIT Kharagpur as the nodal center for the Hardware Edition.Here is everything I learned from those 5 intense, unforgettable days — lessons that no classroom will ever teach you.How It Started — A Software Person Goes Hardware I come from a software background. Python, Flask, web apps — that is my comfort zone. So when our team decided to take on the Hardware Edition of SIH, it was a deliberate challenge. We had already built the project before going in. We had tested it. We were confident. We thought we were ready.We were not.The Most Important Lesson: You Don't Know What They Want Until You Talk to Them Here is the truth nobody tells you before a hackathon — the project you build thinking it is perfect is rarely what the problem statement actually needs.The real breakthrough happens when you talk to the mentors.At IIT Kharagpur, industry mentors were present from the very first day. The biggest mistake a team can make is to stay in their corner, heads down, building. Instead, the first thing you should do is walk up to a mentor and tell them your vision — what problem you are trying to solve and how you are approaching it.They will guide you. They will tell you what the actual plant-level requirements are. They will tell you what industry professionals genuinely need — not what sounds impressive in a pitch, but what makes their job faster, safer, and simpler. Industry mentors do not want complexity. They want solutions that work reliably, with no hassle, every single time.That conversation on Day 1 changed the entire direction of our project.Round 1 — Lead With Your Vision In the first evaluation round, do not lead with features. Lead with the problem.Tell the evaluators clearly:• What exact problem exists today• Why current solutions are failing• What your approach is and why it is different Be honest about what your solution does and does not do. Evaluators at SIH are experienced professionals. They can see through exaggeration immediately. A grounded, clear explanation of your vision will always outperform an over-polished pitch.Round 2 — Show the Work, Validate the Solution By the second round, you have had time to build, iterate, and refine. Now your job is different.Present what you actually built. Walk them through the USPs — the specific things your solution does better than anything else available. But then — and this is the part most teams skip — ask them directly:"Is this actually solving a real problem?"This question sounds risky. It is not. It shows maturity. Sometimes what you are building does not address the actual pain point. Sometimes the problem you are solving does not even exist at the scale you assumed. Finding this out during the hackathon — and correcting course — is far better than winning with a solution nobody will ever use.Your solution must align with the mentor's vision more than your own. That is not a compromise. That is what real-world product thinking looks like.The Hardware Reality — Where Mistakes Are Expensive Our hardware was solid. We had done significant pre-work before arriving at IIT Kharagpur, and that preparation was what put us in the top 5.But here is what I learned about hardware that every software person needs to understand:Software mistakes can be fixed overnight. Hardware mistakes are a different story entirely.A bug in your code — you stay up, you fix it, you redeploy. A mistake in your hardware circuit, your embedded logic, or your physical assembly? That costs you time you do not have, money you may not have budgeted, and in the worst case, it can make your entire prototype unsafe.Last-minute changes in hardware are almost inevitable. Components behave differently under real conditions than in your lab. Always:• Build with safety margins• Have backup components ready• Never make a hardware change in the final hours without testing it first• Prioritize safety over performance, always Make Friends — Seriously Five days at a nodal center with some of the brightest student teams from across India is not just a competition. It is a networking opportunity you will not get again easily.Talk to other teams. Understand what problems they are solving. Share ideas. The people you meet at SIH become your professional network — future colleagues, co-founders, and collaborators.Some of my best conversations at IIT Kharagpur happened not during evaluations but during the breaks between rounds.Key Takeaways• Talk to mentors on Day 1. Tell them your vision before you start building blindly.• Understand actual industry requirements — speed, safety, simplicity matter more than features.• In Round 1, lead with the problem. In Round 2, show the work and validate the solution.• Ask mentors if your solution is actually useful. Be open to pivoting.• Align your solution with the mentor's vision, not just your own.• Pre-work matters enormously. Arrive prepared.• In hardware, last-minute changes are risky. Always prioritize safety.• Build connections with other teams. The friendships are worth as much as the trophy.Final Thoughts Making it to the top 5 out of 500+ teams at Smart India Hackathon 2024 was one of the most defining experiences of my engineering journey. Not because of the ranking — but because of what those 5 days taught me about building real solutions for real people.If you are preparing for SIH or any hardware hackathon, go in with your best work. But go in even more prepared to listen, adapt, and rebuild. That is where the real learning lives.Comment Corporate & Communications Address:A-143, 6th Floor, Sovereign Corporate Tower, Sector- 136, Noida, Uttar Pradesh (201305)Registered Address:K 061, Tower K, Gulshan Vivante Apartment, Sector 137, Noida, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, 201305Company About Us Legal Privacy Policy Careers Contact Us Corporate Solution Campus Training Program Explore POTDPractice Problems Blogs Upskill Courses Connect Tutorials Programming Languages DSAWeb Technology AI, ML & Data Science Dev Ops CS Core Subjects GATESchool Subjects Software and Tools Courses ML and Data Science DSA and Placements Web Development Data Science Programming Languages Dev Ops & Cloud GATEMongo DB Certifications Preparation Corner Interview Corner Aptitude Puzzles Gf G 160System Design@Geeksfor Geeks, Sanchhaya Education Private Limited, All rights reserved

My name is Ajith Kumar Reddy, and I completed my B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering from Vel Tech, Chennai, in 2025. I appeared for the TCS Digital hiring process through the TCS NQT Off-Campus Drive 2025 and applied via the TCS Next Step Portal. The entire selection process, from the initial assessment to the final confirmation, took approximately 12 to 14 months. All the rounds in the TCS selection process were elimination-based, meaning candidates had to clear each stage successfully to progress to the next round.Round 1 – Online Assessment (180-190 mins) :After a couple of weeks of applying, I received an invitation to attend the TCS i ON centre online assessment. The exam was conducted in a proctored environment at the TCS i ON centre and served as the first screening stage.The TCS NQT exam consisted of a foundation section and an advanced section. The Foundation Section included Numerical Ability with 25 minutes and 20 questions Verbal Ability with 25 minutes and 25 questions, and Reasoning Ability with 25 minutes and 20 questions. The Advanced Section included Advanced Quantitative and Reasoning Ability with 25 minutes and around 14–16 questions, and Advanced coding with 90 minutes and 2 coding questions. The overall exam duration was 190 minutes with approximately 82 questions. In the coding section, multiple programming languages such as C, C++, Java, and Python were allowed. The exam tested both aptitude fundamentals and advanced problem-solving skills, especially in coding and logical reasoning. The round was moderately difficult and manageable if the basics were strong, and strong time management was very important to complete the test within the given duration.Round 2 – In-Person Interview (30-45 mins) :A couple of months after clearing the online test, I received a score-based selection for the Digital role and was shortlisted for the next round. After some days, I got an interview location mail from TCS and attended the interview at the campus mentioned in the mail. Initially, my documents and background verification forms were checked, which took around 20–30 minutes. After that, I was assigned a panel for the technical and HR discussion. The combined technical and HR interview lasted around 30–45 minutes. The interviewer started with a brief introduction and asked me to introduce myself. He then went through my resume and asked detailed questions about my final year project, internships, and technical skills. They also asked a coding question based on strings and arrays, which I explained confidently. Further, they asked questions from Computer Networks, Operating Systems, Machine Learning, and Data Science concepts. In the HR discussion, the panel also spoke about TCS work culture, company initiatives, and different business units. The panel asked me situational and behavioral questions related to workplace scenarios. Towards the end of the interview, I was given an opportunity to ask questions, where I asked about the day-to-day roles and responsibilities of the position. The interviewer responded positively and explained the expectations in detail.Overall Experience & Tips: The entire process was smooth and well-structured, with all rounds being elimination-based. It is very important to thoroughly revise everything mentioned in your resume, especially your final year project, technical skills, and any internships. Strong knowledge of core CS fundamentals such as Computer Networks, Operating Systems, Data Structures & Algorithms and basic concepts of Machine Learning and Data Science is essential. Coding preparation should mainly focus on arrays and strings, as these are commonly asked. Along with technical preparation, equal importance should be given to aptitude skills and communication, as they play a key role in the initial screening stages. Overall, the interview experience was smooth, structured, and interviewer-friendly, making it comfortable to express my answers clearly. I am sharing my interview experience to help aspiring candidates understand the selection process and prepare more effectively.Round 1: Online Assessment The first round was an online assessment consisting entirely of multiple-choice questions (MCQs).The questions were asked from:- Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs)- DBMS- SQL- Operating Systems- Computer Networks- Java Fundamentals- Data Structures and Algorithms- Aptitude and Logical Reasoning The overall difficulty level was moderate. Most questions were based on fundamental concepts, so having a strong understanding of core computer science subjects was helpful in clearing this round.Round 2: Technical Interview (DSA)The second round was focused entirely on Data Structures and Algorithms.After a brief introduction, the interviewer directly moved to a Dynamic Programming problem based on strings.Problem Statement : Given a query word and a list of words, find the word that is closest to the query word. Closeness was defined using Levenshtein Distance (Edit Distance). If multiple words had the same minimum edit distance, the lexicographically smaller word had to be returned. The interviewer expected me to explain the approach first and then discuss an optimized Dynamic Programming solution.The discussion covered:- Understanding Edit Distance- Recursive approach- Dynamic Programming optimization- DP table construction- Time and Space Complexity analysis- Lexicographical tie-breaking conditions The interviewer focused heavily on my thought process and problem-solving approach rather than just the final code.Overall, this round tested Dynamic Programming concepts, optimization techniques, and analytical thinking.Round 3: Technical Interview (Projects & Experience)This was the deepest and most detailed round of the entire process.The interviewer thoroughly reviewed my resume and asked extensive questions about my projects, internship experiences, responsibilities, and technical contributions.Most of the discussion was based on the actual work I had done during my internships and projects rather than theoretical concepts.The interviewer asked me to explain:- My role and responsibilities- Technologies I had worked with- Features I had implemented- Challenges I faced during development- Debugging and issue-resolution approaches- Design and architectural decisions- Lessons learned from real-world development A significant amount of time was spent discussing the projects mentioned on my resume. The interviewer continuously asked follow-up questions to assess the depth of my understanding and verify my contributions. There was also a discussion around Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning concepts. The questions were basic and focused on understanding AI/ML applications and concepts.My advice for this round is to know every single point written on your resume because the interviewer can go very deep into your projects and experiences.Round 4: HR + Managerial Round The final round was a combination of HR and managerial discussion.The interviewer asked standard HR questions such as:- Tell me about yourself.- Why do you want to join Broadridge?- What are your strengths and weaknesses?- Are you willing to relocate?- Where do you see yourself in the next few years?Apart from these, I was also asked a few logical and situational questions to evaluate my analytical thinking and decision-making abilities.The discussion focused on:- Logical reasoning- Problem-solving ability- Team collaboration- Workplace scenarios- Communication skills- Handling challenging situations The overall interaction was friendly and conversational.Result : A few days after completing the interview process, I received confirmation that I had been been selected for the Member Technical role at Broadridge.Final Thoughts : My overall interview experience was very positive and well-structured. Each round focused on a different aspect of evaluation, including technical fundamentals, coding ability, project knowledge, practical experience, logical reasoning, and communication skills.Some key takeaways for future candidates: - Strengthen your core computer science fundamentals. - Practice Dynamic Programming and other DSA topics regularly. - Be prepared to explain your projects and internship work in detail. - Revise OOPs, DBMS, SQL, Operating Systems, and Computer Networks thoroughly. - Have a basic understanding of AI/ML concepts. - Communicate your thought process clearly during interviews.The most important lesson I learned was that interviewers pay significant attention to the projects and experiences mentioned on your resume. Make sure you genuinely understand everything you have listed because follow-up questions can go very deep.I hope this interview experience helps future candidates preparing for Broadridge.
